digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate, context-limit escalation and sizing
propositions: models_at_or_above and largest_window_tokens mishandle non-Anthropic-family primary models by substring-matching only against Anthropic names in MODEL_LADDER, causing unlocated primaries to fall through to the whole ladder or maximum window instead of an explicit outcome
Context-limit escalation for a non-Anthropic primary incorrectly proposes claude-haiku-4-5 as the first rung, crossing provider family and reducing window from the configured model

largest_window_tokens returns MODEL_LADDER[-1][1] (1000000 tokens) for an unlocated primary, overstating the context window and causing P8 under-blocking, resulting in silent truncation instead of explicit too-big findings
Prerequisite-coverage escalation at prerequisites.py:260-263 inherits the same defect, jumping from the operator's model to claude-haiku-4-5 when the ladder cannot locate the primary

Fix requires returning [model] from models_at_or_above for truthy-but-unlocated primaries, preserving single-criterion retry, and returning min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER) from largest_window_tokens for the same case

The fix is isolated to the unlocated case; falsy models and located Anthropic primaries retain existing behavior, and no cross-file edits to prerequisites.py are needed due to existing exception handling
